summary.name: Squarespace Site Reliability Engineering
summary.one_liner: An engineering blog post describing how Squarespace keeps its website-hosting platform reliable through data center design, continuous deployment, monitoring, and incident response.
keywords: how do big sites avoid outages
use_cases: Learning how a large website platform handles uptime and outages
Reviewing SRE practices such as monitoring, alerting, and postmortems
Understanding automated deployment pipelines with staging smoke tests
Benchmarking monitoring and logging scale at a SaaS company
summary.what_it_does: The post describes Squarespace's reliability approach across several areas. Infrastructure runs across geographically distributed data centers, provisioned with Ansible as code, with disaster-recovery mechanisms to shift traffic and replicate data. Code goes through automated builds, tests, QA environments, a staging smoke-test run, and then production, with 5 to 12 main-application deployments per weekday. Monitoring uses Graphite, ELK, and Zipkin, plus Sensu for alerting and PagerDuty for customer-impacting issues. The post also covers CDNs, HTTP/2, automatic SSL/TLS certificates, a custom web-application firewall, DDoS defenses, and monthly operational-excellence reporting.
notable: Deploys the main application 5 to 12 times per weekday through an automated pipeline
Ingests over 14 million metrics per minute into Graphite and 1 million log lines per minute into ELK
Weekly organization-wide postmortem review every Friday
caveats: This is a description of internal practices from a 2017 blog post, not a product users can download or license
Specific figures and tool choices may be out of date
